physics_goals.quote: We report a measurement of the positive muon lifetime to a precision of 1.0 parts per million (ppm); it is the most precise particle lifetime ever measured.
physics_goals.value: Measure the positive muon lifetime to part-per-million precision to determine the Fermi constant

summary.plain: An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute that timed billions of muon decays with a ring of scintillator detectors. It gave the muon’s lifetime to one part in a million, the most precise lifetime of any particle, and from it the strength of the weak force.
summary.technical: MuLan at PSI (pi E3 beamline, 590 MeV cyclotron): time-structured, nearly 100% polarized surface muon beam stopping in ferromagnetic and quartz targets, segmented fast-timing scintillator array; muon lifetime 2196980.3(2.2) ps (1.0 ppm), Fermi constant G_F = 1.1663787(6) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.5 ppm). Data 2004, 2006-2007.
